agent_note: First-person present-tense narration, simultaneous rather than retrospective: events are reported as they occur ('I meet Silas at the movie theater on Church Street', 'I put my key in the lock', 'I open the cookie tin'). 45 event quotes, 38 present / 7 past (84.4% present). The past minority is not diary duality - there is no entry structure, no dating, no writing-moment frame. It is a recollection strand: dead mother, ended relationships, and earlier days at the novel (q00584, q00585, q00597, q00606, q00612, q00620, q00563), embedded as memory inside a present-tense base narration. At 7/45 = 15.6% it does not reach the 25% split threshold, so it should not trigger SPLIT_REVIEW. Note that 84.4% present sits just under the 85% high-confidence-present bar, and a single reassignment moves it either way - q00563 is the pivot (present would give 86.7%). Heavy gnomic load as predicted for a book about writing: 12 gnomic of 65, mostly second-person universals and aphorisms about writing, reading, men, and fear. Two dialogue quotes (q00595, q00607) have no quotation marks in the Goodreads excerpt but are unmistakably speech in a scene; two more (q00594, q00599) are dialogue only by the new precedence rule, since each carries a narration beat that the older tag rule would have promoted to event/present.
